result.title: SepsisLens: Structure-Preserving Sequence Modelling for Decomposable Early Sepsis Warning
result.summary: Early sepsis warning from ICU records can be cast as a structure-preserving prediction problem. A model needs to detect deterioration from irregular measurements while keeping each alert connected to the physiological signals that support it. Many temporal models fuse clinical variables into a patient-level representation, supporting scalar risk prediction but weakening the structure needed for clinical decomposition. We present SepsisLens, which preserves variable-indexed temporal states until risk composition. Observation-aware representations encode each variable's dynamics and measurement history, while a shared temporal encoder models each trajectory without collapsing the variable axis. The StructuredRiskHead composes multi-horizon risk from explicit variable-level and organ-level components. We evaluate SepsisLens on three public ICU cohorts and one private-hospital cohort under a common pre-onset protocol. SepsisLens achieves strong discrimination on all four cohorts and lower alert burden at matched event recall on MIMIC-IV. Structural ablations support the design, while input-side masking shows that the ranked components reflect variables with greater influence on prediction.

AI.brief_summary: SepsisLens 面向 ICU 早期脓毒症预警，通过在风险合成前保留变量索引的时间状态，让每次警报可分解到具体的生理信号与器官级成分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构保持」思路与 LVR 关心的内部状态是否保留实体/变量级信息、以及预测是否真正使用这些成分有概念联系，但属临床时序预测，可作为状态抽象与可分解监督的借鉴线索，需核查。
